output.question: What class action lawsuits has Synchrony Bank faced?
output.answer: Synchrony Bank, and its parent Synchrony Financial, has faced several class actions. The best-documented is a shareholder securities case, In re Synchrony Financial Securities Litigation (D. Conn., No. 3:18-cv-01818). It alleged that Synchrony misrepresented its underwriting standards and concealed strain in its relationships with retail partners such as Walmart during a class period from Jan. 19 to July 12, 2018. It settled for $34 million in cash, approved on Aug. 4, 2023, with final judgment on Aug. 7, 2023. Synchrony's SEC filings also report consumer class actions. These include the Campbell/Neal suits under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), a federal law on automated calls; the consolidated case got final settlement approval on March 19, 2021. They also include a bankruptcy-court class action over credit reporting of sold accounts, settled for up to $8.5 million with final approval in February 2022, and the earlier Abdeljalil TCPA class settlement from 2016. Search results also show a new 2026 TCPA robocall complaint over prerecorded debt-collection calls, a $2.6M TCPA settlement over calls to people who weren't the account holder, and an August 2024 New York suit claiming CareCredit's 32.99% rate breaks state usury law. I couldn't open those pages to confirm them.

key_facts.fact: In the securities class action (D. Conn., Case No. 3:18-cv-01818), the class period was Jan. 19 to July 12, 2018. Plaintiffs alleged Synchrony overstated its underwriting discipline, relaxed its standards, and hid strained retail-partner relationships, including with Walmart.
The securities case settled for $34,000,000 in cash. The court approved it on Aug. 4, 2023 and entered final judgment on Aug. 7, 2023.

The Campbell/Neal TCPA class actions, consolidated in the W.D. North Carolina, settled. Preliminary approval came on Oct. 19, 2020 and final approval on March 19, 2021. This comes from search-result snippets of Synchrony's SEC filings; I couldn't open the legal-proceedings section.

In a bankruptcy-court class action over credit reporting of sold accounts, the Bank agreed to pay up to $8.5 million. Final approval came in February 2022. This comes from a search-result snippet of an SEC filing.

The Abdeljalil TCPA class action, filed in 2012 against predecessor GE Capital Retail Bank, received preliminary settlement approval on June 16, 2016. This comes from a search-result snippet of an SEC filing.

passages.quote: On March 19, 2021, the District Court granted final approval of the settlement and entered final judgment and order of dismissal.
the Bank will pay up to $8.5 million to class members, and implement or maintain certain practices with respect to credit reporting of sold accounts

caveats.caveat: The SEC filing quotes and dates come from search-result snippets. WebFetch truncated the filings before their legal-proceedings sections, so I couldn't confirm them on the page itself.

The 2026 TCPA robocall complaint (injuryclaims.com, updated June 30, 2026, court not confirmed) and the $2.6M prerecorded-call settlement (topclassactions.com, undated) both returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't verify them.
The August 2024 CareCredit usury suit came from a search summary that seemed to rely on Wikipedia. I didn't open the source and found no outcome.
I couldn't check Synchrony's latest 2026 10-Q or 10-K legal disclosures, so newer or still-pending class actions may be missing.
Some of these cases name Synchrony Financial, the parent, rather than Synchrony Bank. The securities suit, for example, was brought by shareholders against the parent.
